If I could make one change to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, it would be to disable that new swipe-down gesture for summoning Siri AI. There are already enough ways to summon Siri, and it won't disrupt my muscle memory for opening Notification Center on my iPhone and iPad.

Meanwhile, on the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even in late August, new betas are still adding welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one change I'd like to see.

MacBook battery percentage is harder to read in macOS 27 Golden Gate

macOS 27 Golden Gate includes a redesigned menu bar battery control. By default, the percentage isn't shown—only a battery-shaped visual indicator.

In that state, it looks fine. I also turn off the percentage display on my iPhone, which has the same kind of battery indicator. However, I've always preferred to show the percentage on my Mac.

If you turn on the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number is placed inside the battery icon. I assume this is for consistency with what iPhone is doing in iOS 27.

Putting the percentage inside the battery icon on iPhone was a density solution Apple adopted to address cramped space to the right of the notch or Dynamic Island. But on the Mac, even in the menu bar, I don't have that kind of screen space problem.

I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15″ MacBook Air since the first developer beta. I've found that I'm generally paying less attention to my battery percentage, because it's harder for my eyes to make out.

I hope Apple will reconsider this design decision in the future, especially if it's bothering more users. In the meantime, I've at least solved the problem for myself.

I used Codex to make a simple menu bar utility that reliably shows the current battery status and percentage with the visual clarity I'd expect. If it helps you too, you can download and install it for free here.
